utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Semenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Vucicevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Semenovic. Mr. Semenovic, you testified in the Tadic case and also you gave a statement in this case about the date when you met with SDS officers and the military commanders of Prijedor. In the Tadic case you said it was 16th, and then in Tadic case you said it was eight days before, another answer was eight days before the attack began, and then you said in this case, it was 15th to 18th. Could you please reconcile those dates for the Court?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When answering that question, I clarified that I could not give the exact date because I had not remembered the exact dates, but I gave it a time frame, when this meeting took place, and I said that it was after the 16th or eight days before the attack, so that refers to the same period because the attack on Kozarac was on the 24th, but at any rate, the meeting took place within that time period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the meeting itself that was held in the offices of SDS in Prijedor, you testified that Mr. Kurnoga was there, Mr. Kuruzovic was there, and the meeting couldn't get started before the military commanders came over; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Miskovic said that the meeting could only start after Mr. Zeljaja and Mr. Arsic arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Miskovic's position in the SDS at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the president of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified in the Tadic trial that about half an hour later, Mr. Zeljaja, Lieutenant-Colonel Arsic, and another soldier or a military officer whom you did not know arrived; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody else arrive with them?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not remember whether anybody else arrived with them. There were some persons present there previously, and I had mentioned them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... that were present in the room, before the meeting commenced?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I already stated that Kuruzovic was present as well as Miskovic, Dusan Kurnoga was present, and there were another one or two persons whom I did not know, they were in civilian clothes. I assumed they were not members from the SDS leadership, but I do not know these persons so I could not tell you who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say you knew all the leadership of the Prijedor SDS by that time, having been in a coalition government with them?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not know all the SDS leadership because the leadership of every party consisted of a number of people who had at least eleven members. The SDS changes leadership at least two or three times. It was impossible to remember all these names. I only knew the persons with whom I had some direct type of contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please -- you have testified in the Tadic trial that Major Zeljaja told delegation from Kozarac to return 7.000 rifles. Then when you testified on Wednesday, you testified that Colonel Arsic told the delegation to return 5.000 rifles. Could you reconcile who said that and how many rifles indeed were demanded for return?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I recall, Zeljaja said 5.000 rifles, and when Mr. Arsic referred to his intelligence officer who was sitting right next to him, the figure was put at 7.000, and for the entire Prijedor, I think the total number was 11.000. I do not know the exact number, but I know that it was over 10.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made a demand or made an estimate that there was over 10.000 rifles in Kozarac on or about May 16, 1992, at the meeting in the SDS offices?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nobody estimated that the number referred to Kozarac, but in the area of the Prijedor municipality. This is what Colonel Arsic was referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to a statement made by Lieutenant-Colonel Arsic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, all their statements were important to us, not only at that time but even before, because we had been accused of something for which there was no evidence, and since these were accusations against us, we deemed them very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... you testified to that statement in Tadic's trial, didn't you, that there was ten to eleven thousand rifles according to Lieutenant-Colonel Arsic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I do not remember whether I said that or not. That meeting took place -- it was a long one, and what I was saying at that time was answers to questions that were asked and I was not in a position to say -- to state the entire event, and this is one of a large number of meetings which I attended before, during, and after the election process, so in that short period of time, it would have been impossible to interpret all of this, and even when you're asked questions, you cannot recall all the details. This is why you need a discussion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems it would be very important to distinguish political dialogue in the meetings and testifying in the court, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a matter of comment, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I will withdraw that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Tadic's trial, you testified that Mr. Medunjanin made a comment about the number of the rifles. What was the number of rifles that Mr. Medunjanin mentioned. Your Honours, I will direct you to the Tadic transcript, page 924.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this moment, I cannot remember the number mentioned by Mr. Medunjanin. I spoke about that two years ago, so it has been two years since that time. I only know that he spoke about a much, much smaller number of weapons than the number for which we had been originally accused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So today you don't remember what you said two years ago; isn't that correct? And today you don't remember what Mr. Medunjanin said seven years ago -- six years ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, first I would object. Counsel is misstating the record. If he is going to refer to the record, I assume he is asking that this be admitted as evidence for consideration by the Trial Chamber, and in which case he is misquoting the evidence given by the witness, because at the time -- it's actually 923 on the transcript I have, the conversation which I believe he's referring to, and in which case Mr. Medunjanin was simply responding to --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting to this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let Mr. Keegan -- let Mr. Keegan finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Of course, the testing of memory is a legitimate avenue but not when you're misquoting the witness which then misleads the witness, and can put the witness into conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the quotation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: There's nothing on 924, I believe it's on 923, the conversation, and Mr. Medunjanin didn't refer to them having a specific number of weapons, he was simply responding and said, "How can we give you 7.000 when there's not even a thousand?" So Mr. Medunjanin did not refer to a particular number of weapons, which is exactly what the witness is saying, and yet counsel is asserting that there is somehow a difference in the witness's testimony when there, in fact, isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not, at the moment, going to ask the Trial Chamber to consider any question of admitting some previous statement as evidence. No doubt we can consider such an application in due course. But clearly counsel is entitled to cross-examine about earlier evidence. I do wonder, Mr. Vucicevic, about how helpful it is for a witness to be cross-examined as to precisely what he said two years ago and whether he remembers what he said two years ago. It would be surprising if he did. Put any inconsistencies, by all means, to the witness, but I don't think we're going to be helped by a detailed recital of what the witness said or didn't say in Tadic. Can we move on now --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you to comment, Mr. Vucicevic, I'm asking you to move on, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, I am directing your attention to your testimony in Tadic's trial, page 923, line 14, and I will read this for you, sir, verbatim. The question was: Did Commander Zeljaja indicate what he would do if 7.000 weapons were not turned over to SDS? Your answer was: Yes, he did. After these words of his, Mr. Medunjanin asked to speak and then Mr. Tadic. They said it was impossible to surrender 7.000 rifles when there was not even a thousand of them. Do you remember speaking these words?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, now whether the witness remembers or not, that is what the transcript says in the Tadic trial. Now, Mr. Semenovic, is that the position or not? Did Mr. Medunjanin say something along those lines?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Something along those lines, but the number of pieces of weapons, he did not specify. He did not say a precise number. He wanted to say that there was not even an approximate number of the ones we were accused of. Now you have just reminded me. He said something to that effect. He did not say that Kozarac had about 1.000, he said, in fact, Kozarac did not have even 1.000. Those were his words. Of course, I testified two years ago, and I did not have an opportunity to read or review this testimony of mine, so that when I'm asked a question, I need to refresh my memory, I need to recall these events and what the gentleman is asking me about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, when you testified yesterday, you quoted Mr. Medunjanin that there was no more than 5.000 rifles?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, I'm going to instruct you to move on. You've dealt with this point, you've drawn our attention to what it said in Tadic. I don't think we're going to get much further.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I was just, you know, pointing inconsistencies, you know, two years versus yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can make all those points in due course. Can we move on now to something else, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, in the Tadic trial, right at the beginning, when you began discussing your political career, page 892, line 1. In answer to the question "Did you become involved in the political process at this time?" You said, "Yes, I became politically active as of the second half of 1989." In your testimony yesterday, you said you began your political career, you became politically active as of the middle of 1990. Could you reconcile those two answers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think you asked him yesterday about this. That's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I intentionally, after hearing his answer, I intentionally omitted his reference to Tadic's trial. I think the record -- my recollection is clear, the record would reflect it. That's why I'm asking him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I don't think we ought to go back to all that again. You cross-examined about it very fully yesterday. Can we go on, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, when you testified yesterday, when the SDA was formed, you also indicated that the presiding officer, the chairman of SDA, on the State level, was Mr. Alija Izetbegovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also testified a few days ago that SDA had a programme, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Every party had its own programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did Mr. Alija Izetbegovic become the president of the SDA or the chairman, whatever the proper translation might be?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I gave that answer yesterday. When the SDA was officially established, that was sometime in June in 1992 -- in the '90s. That is when it was registered and that's when its founding conference was held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... founding declaration written by Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did. A lot was said about that. It was covered in the media, and Mr. Izetbegovic was very much in focus. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has Mr. Izetbegovic written any other books, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that he wrote very few books, but I did not read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would like to tender the next Defence Exhibit. Just different national practice. Your Honours, I didn't get a chance because I got this book a couple days ago. I didn't get a chance to translate it. But I will read -- I will ask the witness to read a pertinent paragraph, and you will get a translation. In a couple of days, I will translate and tender to you the full translation of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will allow you to do it, but normally, you must understand, the Rules are these documents have to appear translated. As an exception, we will let you do it on this occasion, but in future, could you make sure it is translated, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, I'm directing your attention to the page 22, the last paragraph, starting with "First and most important of these conclusions," first two sentences.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you read it out loud so that the Court -- the interpreters would interpret that for the Judges to hear what is being written there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean to quote the text?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here it states, and I quote: "First and most important of these conclusions and I did not read what these conclusions were, so the first and most important of these conclusions is the irreconcilability of Islam and non-Islamic religions, there is no peace between and coexistence between the Islamic and non-Islamic social and political institutions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want the witness to read on, Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want the witness to read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just that passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Just this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with this statement, Mr. Semenovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I do not understand the context of it because I read a quote from a book which I have not read, so I don't know what preceded this quote and what came after it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you simply whether you agree or disagree with the statement that you just read, and I'll repeat it: "There is no peace or coexistence between Islamic faith and non-Islamic social and political institutions."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I absolutely do not agree with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the first annual convention, anniversary of the SDA -- of the SDA of Bosnia-Herzegovina held? I'm directing your attention to a year 1991.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean the first anniversary?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the first annual assembly of the SDA for Bosnia and Herzegovina held, in 1991 being that the establishment was in 1990?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean the first convention or you mean the founding conference?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a meeting held in Foca in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was a meeting in Foca, but it was neither a convention nor the founding conference, it was just a meeting. I heard that on television and I heard from within the party that they supported that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... Mr. Izetbegovic's presentation at that political gathering?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not remember following it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. If I might? This is now approximately about the fifth question or answer that the reporter has not been able to get, the same problem as yesterday, that he is talking over the witness. You will notice in the transcript we are missing the first part of questions. We have also missed answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, did you hear that point made by Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm cognisant of that fact, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you bear that in mind all the time, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, having testified that you disagreed with this statement of the party leader, isn't it fair to conclude that the Prijedor SDA disagreed with the policies of the leadership in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour -- may I object to that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think so. No, you can't object. It's not objectionable. But let's deal with these matters as quickly as we can, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, did the local SDA disagree with the policies of the Sarajevo leadership?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I just want to say that this is not a statement of the president of the party, this is a statement that this man gave 20 or 30 years ago in a book, and this is the book. This book was written several decades before the period of which we are talking, and this is a quote from one book of this man. Many years later he became the president of this party, and he did not give this statement, nor did he officially restate this as president of the party. He was talking -- he talked about this book on a number of occasions, but I was never much interested in that book, I never read it, and it was not part of the programme of the SDA. This is all I can state about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were referring to the arms that were available in Kozarac area, you said there were not enough arms even for one-third of the population.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that that was to illustrate the things that I was referring to before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... you testified and you were shown the exhibits denoting the lists of the Territorial Defence mobilisation, call-up lists. You also testified in Tadic's trial that you participated personally in reinforcement of these lists. Could you tell the Court how many formation units of TO were there in Kozarac and surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know because I was not in charge of Territorial Defence nor was I in charge of the organisation of the Territorial Defence in this military sense based on the laws under which they were established, so I really don't know how many people were involved, how many pieces of weapons there were. It was not part of my duties, simply put. And I don't know these numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that there was on April 8th, there was a letter or directive that came up from the Republic level indicating the call-up, mobilisation of the Territorial Defence. Do you know who issued that order?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that as far as I recall this was on the 8th, so it was probably on the 8th of April, but I'm not sure about it. However, what I am sure of is that it was an order of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The territorial staff of the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established and this decision was read on the radio, anybody could have heard it. I think that also Croatian television carried it as well as some others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was on April the 8th, State of Bosnia and Herzegovina called up all its armed forces which it had on its command; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It issued an order on mobilisation of Territorial Defence, and I mentioned this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Prijedor, SDA committee implemented that order on the Muslim populated and dominated area, isn't that correct, by setting up the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. There was a Territorial Defence command in Prijedor, and it was in charge of implementing this order. However, it had a mixed ethnic composition, and the relationship between the leaders of Serbian ethnic background -- I have already explained their position in view of this. So in this context and in view of these relationships, this order could not be implemented because part of the people did not accept this order. I said that this order from -- this order could not be implemented completely in Prijedor, which meant that in a part of Prijedor, a decision of the Presidency of the State cannot be implemented. Some people started implementing parts of this decision; however, it was not very successful because the central coordination was lacking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a politician from -- living in Trnopolje, a politician for the whole municipality. You were indeed very concerned when this order came down, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was concerned even before this order because daily we watched events that I have already described in my testimony, there were explosions, shootings, and everybody was concerned at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified that JNA tank was positioned on or about May 3rd at the intersection of the main road from Prijedor to Banja Luka, so-called Banja Luka Cesta, and the main side road that is going into Kozarac; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, it was on May 3rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time was there a checkpoint by Kozarac or just on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think yes. After the tank appeared, people created this checkpoint and sort of protection -- sort of a shelter, I think it was made out of wood or sand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically JNA soldiers on one side of the road and SDA army, TO, from the other side, were staring at each other across the road, down the gun barrel?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those were not the JNA soldiers, it was mainly the known persons -- well-known persons and people from Kozarac even talked to them. I have in mind soldiers that were around the tank and the crew of the tank. Those were people, older people from Kozarac and from the area who served their army service a long time ago, and this happened after the take-over of the power by SDS in Prijedor, three days after that take-over, the tank appeared there, and the population was just basically taken by -- overcome by panic and they tried to create some kind of shelter for themselves, protection. You said on one side there was TO and on the other side was the JNA. No, it was not the JNA. We could clearly recognise the soldiers of the JNA. At that point, part of the soldiers of JNA were in Benkovac in the military camp, and we know that because many of them wanted to escape and they would apply to people in Kozarac, and some of the people in Kozarac would help them and procure a civilian wardrobe so they could escape. There was an example, a baker, Jevid, provided clothes for several soldiers of the JNA so they could escape. Another example is Avdo Mujkanovic. He also assisted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: ... from in a intersection that I just asked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it fair to say that from April the 8th, there was a state of Cold War in Bosnia between SDA and SDS based on what you just testified?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand the term "Cold War," the state of Cold War. We were issued an ultimatum, and prior to that, the officials in their discussions and on the radio broadcast, after the take-over, they were issuing messages and saying -- stating that very clearly, they want disarmament of extremists, and after that the tanks appeared and things were obvious. If you wish to ask me if, on one side, there was a checkpoint of TO and on the other side was the tank, yes, that's clear. It's an obvious matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on or about May 16th, when you and the other officials from Kozarac were issued ultimatum by the JNA commanders, you go back to Kozarac and discuss that ultimatum with anybody?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you discuss it with, when and where, location? Who was present?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date. I think it was a day after this meeting in Prijedor. A meeting was called, a mass meeting was called, and there were representatives of the local communes there, police and Territorial Defence representatives, all of them came and the meeting was held in the building of the elementary school in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody else speak at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Becir Medunjanin spoke as well. Many people spoke. It was a meeting that lasted for several hours, because after these threats, it was obvious people would be killed and we looked for a solution. Many people spoke and I really cannot remember the names of 20 or 30 people that did speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Basically choice was either to surrender the arms or go to war, to shooting war. What did you recommend?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. The choice was to surrender the weapons and to have the Serbian police enter Kozarac and raise the Serbian flag. That was what we were asked to allow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ... for the gathering at the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not have a proposal. I interpreted what I had heard at that meeting that I've mentioned. People were called to the meeting to discuss this and to make a decision. I did not suggest anything at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what Mr. Medunjanin said at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember quite well those speeches, but I know that Medunjanin didn't have a specific proposal either. The purpose of that meeting was to make some kind of a common -- issue some kind of a common decision; however, not to pass the decision by an official or an official of the TO or a politician. If we had wanted to do that, we wouldn't call upon the people to come to the meeting. The purpose of the meeting was to have a large number of people make a common decision that would be supported by everybody, and if I remember correctly, Becir Medunjanin did not say "We will do this and this" or "We should do this and that." He simply called the meeting in order to ask what was the will of the people present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That was an example. The interpreter hadn't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I may have to insist in due course that you put the ear phones on so you can hear, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It may be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, was there a question put to the assembly on the issue whether to surrender the arms and accept the Serbian authority in Kozarac or not? Was there a vote taken on that issue by the assembly of people?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but I do think that there was some kind of expression of opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was indeed a very important meeting and this seemed to be a democratic process taking place. If I may follow up with the same line of questioning?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, there was indeed an important issue debated. One of the most important issues in the life of all politicians from that area. And SDS and SDA advised and supported democratic processes. How was a decision reached at that meeting and what was the decision?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The decision at the meeting was for us to abide by the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina because we did not recognise the State that was created by the Serbs. They had already by that time created Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they wanted this part to become a part of the Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina, and at the end, the decision was made to follow the instructions of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina and of our authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the direction by your authorities which you followed on the point of ultimatum that was before you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We did not have any contact with our authorities in the Republic, we had no telephone communication or any other means of communication. The only thing we had were the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we had a Territorial Defence as a structural organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we had police in Kozarac as a structural organisation set up by the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's all that we had. And we also listened to radio broadcasts, we heard the statements by the officials and the views taken by the presidency. We had two options, either to stop -- cease being Bosnia-Herzegovina and agree to enter the newly created Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina or to remain Bosnia and Herzegovina, and people decided to remain in Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was the decision reached at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, you were informed that Kozarac was encircled. Based on information received before, you knew the location and the strength of the military that was opposing you and their artillery, the numbers, and it seems the decision before you and the people of Kozarac is not to defend independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that point, but to decide whether to fight or not or to surrender. Could you narrow your answer to that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can tell you the following concerning that issue: People had decided -- of course, everyone was afraid for their lives. We were aware that we were completely surrounded and we decided to continue to exist as Bosnia and Herzegovina because only as such we had a right to legal defence, lawful defence. Also at that time there was a decision issued by JNA to withdraw from Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was broadcast on the radio. The Security Council of the U.N. also made a resolution concerning the aggression in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we expected that despite this huge military force that was around us, we believed that in view of this decision, resolution by the International Community, that the attack would be prevented and we thought it was just a matter of a few days when this decision on withdrawal would be upheld, and, of course, at that time we just wanted to make sure that we did not provoke any action. The decision at that meeting was to abide by the legislation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and to maybe protect ourselves legally should we be attacked. And the decision was, should we be attacked, to defend ourselves, and the only way people could defend themselves was through the Territorial Defence because that was the only remnant of our defence structure under the auspices of the President of the Republic. Everywhere around us was the new state of the Bosnian Serbs that they had created.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, I am bringing you back right to that meeting in Kozarac that you described earlier. Have you, in your address to the meeting, spoke these words that you spoke before the Court about international situation and imminent international developments while facing the ultimatum? Have you spoken about this same issue that you just informed the Court? Your Honour, if I may instruct the witness to just answer "Yes" or "No" and I'll follow up very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So perhaps you could have spoken about this at that time, could you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have testified that you had volunteered for the TO. What was your military assignment or fighting assignment in TO before the fighting started on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't have any special duties. I was placed -- I was a member of TO at their service and I didn't have any particular duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the president of the local board of the SDA in Prijedor at that time, in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dr. Mirza Mujadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you consulted him after the ultimatum was given to you on the 16th of May?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it wasn't possible to establish any kind of connection anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know perhaps where he was at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I knew where he lived and where his house was, but I didn't know where he was at that point. I didn't know if he was at home or some place else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that Mr. Medunjanin guaranteed to military commanders that the Moslem side or Territorial Defence shall not open fire first.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He said in Kozarac it is definite that nobody would shoot at your army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yet the fire was opened at Hambarine checkpoint on the 22nd of May; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard that on the radio. However, I wasn't present in that part of Prijedor, and I don't know what, in fact, did happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly what you heard on the radio at that time about the military confrontation at Hambarine checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly, but on the radio they said something that there was fire, some shooting, somebody was shooting at the Serbian army, and I think it was information of the Crisis Staff, I don't remember exactly because we were in Kozarac, we were surrounded, and we had no physical contact with that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any ultimatums given to the Hambarine TO over the radio shortly thereafter after the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. As far as I remember, some kind of ultimatum was mentioned in that news, but I cannot remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the military activities on Kozarac on the 24th, have you managed at all to go to Kozarac in the next day or two or three?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I tried once, but then after that, no, there was no opportunity for that after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been in any contact with the political leadership of SDA after 22nd of May? And I'm directing your attention only for the three months of 1992, summer months.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I had no contact. I only met a gentleman, his name was Besim Alic who was in the Territorial Defence staff, and I met him mid-July. I already mentioned that I had remained completely alone in that area where I was hiding, and at that time I met this gentleman, Mr. Alic. We had a very brief conversation, two or three sentences, and he said that he's going over the mountain of Kozara and he left and I have never seen him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this might be a good time to adjourn because we will have a tape for the continuation of the hearing or I can go for another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, that's a convenient moment. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may point out to the exhibit that we introduced earlier titled "Islamska Deklaracija," "Islamic Declaration," that publication was -- here is the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. What was the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: And the book, the publication was by small Muslim library, that's the publishing house that's published in Sarajevo in 1990, for your inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will admit the exhibit when it is translated. Yes, Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: The second point, when the -- I pursued a line of questioning on the meeting that took place after the ultimatum was issued by the military commanders, and the meeting took place in Kozarac. I noted the witness used the word "consensus" and translation was made "a decision," and I'd just like to pose a question just to clarify that point, Your Honour. That was pointed out to me by co-counsel during the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, when you testified about the ending phase of the meeting that took place at the elementary school in Kozarac, was there a vote taken?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that there was some kind of expression of will, and I do not remember what exact kind of expression of will, but the point was for the people that came to the meeting, to express their opinion on a common view, common position, with respect to the problems that surrounded them. I don't remember if they voted by raising their hands or it was some kind of a collective expression of will, I really don't remember. I stated that before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just referred to collective expression of will. Could you explain, what do you mean? How is that being done?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There is voting where you make the ballots with the voting lists and then you put the questions on the list and then you put it in the ballot boxes and there is voting conducted in such a way that peoples names are called up and people get up and they say "Yes" or "No." There is also a type of voting where all the people gathered there are asked, "Do you agree with this proposed solution?" And then everybody who is for it raised their hands and those who are against it that don't raise their hands, and then you establish whether you have a majority, whether everybody voted, whether you had enough people for or against it, and this is all different type of voting. I know that we didn't have ballots, this is not how we voted at that meeting. It was some kind of other means of expression of will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So today you clearly explained several modes by which the people could express their vote, informed decision, but you also testified that you really don't remember which one of these means was used.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember if people's names were called out one by one or all of those who were present there were asked whether they agree and they had to raise their hands, I don't remember because in the years prior to that, I participated in a lot of types of voting and I really don't remember which kind of voting took place at what meeting. It would be impossible to remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it fair to state this was one of the most important meetings in your life? Wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were several most important meetings in my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this one you just do not remember, do you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir. We were under terrible pressure, we lived in fear, and we arranged that meeting fearing for our lives, so I think you can understand how we felt at that point. It was a question of whether we will survive or be killed, and we also had to decide how to avoid the mass murder that we saw on TV was taking place in other municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Semenovic. I will move on, Your Honours. Mr. Semenovic, in Trnopolje, did you have any family members who lived in the same house with you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My mother was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go in hiding immediately after the military action started in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that yesterday. On the second day after the mass exodus started from Trnopolje, I started hiding so that people would not suffer if the military who was approaching were with me, because in the eyes of these Serbian authorities, I was an extremist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your mother during that period of time? Could you tell the Court?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean in those days or later, during the entire period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both, both.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you please specify? My mother also started hiding. First she was in the village of Sivci with a group of -- large group of people, then she had to leave that house, and she wandered about through the forests and across the fields, and she herself did not know where she was going, exactly, and somehow she managed to get to Prijedor through Garevci, which was a Serbian area. This is an elderly woman who can barely read and write. She found a person in Prijedor who hid her there and then sent her to the village of Cejreci. From the village of Cejreci, together with some other women, she went to Hambarine. When the Serbian authorities gathered women and children and put them on buses in order to transport them, she was among them and they were transferred to Trnopolje in a convoy. There they spent one night, and the following morning, on these buses and trucks, they took them to Travnik, that is to the village of Turbe which was under the control of the Bosnian army. In Prijedor, it was Muharema Trnjanin's wife who helped her hide, and I don't know about other names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your mother ever inquired about your whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court about that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned that my mother was in the village of Cejreci with a large group of people, and a couple of days later, the people started fearing her because she was the mother of a Muslim extremist, as the Serbian authorities called me, and so they asked her to leave this house, which is the house of Osman Sivac. So she left the house. She wandered in the fields, she was hiding there. Then she went back to the house to pick up some things because she realised she had to flee, and she did not have personal effects that she needed to take along. And so she went to the house -- this was our house now -- and they -- according to what she said, four Serbian soldiers came, they came in a car, they surrounded the house, two of them stayed outside and two of them entered. They mistreated her there, they threatened her, they put the barrel of their rifle in her mouth, and after that, they took her to the car. Leading her to the car, they opened the back door, and she is very short, she's only 150-plus centimetres, and the car was parked next to the vineyard and there was some bushes, and she ran and hid down in the creek. They went looking for her, they shot around, they searched through the garden, they searched through the little forest; however, she was in that creek which had a lot of undergrowth and she went upstream and fled. So this was going on during that day. What she told me. And part of these events were witnessed by some other people who later related it to me. Later on, I received information that she had been killed because some people observed when she was led out of the house, and later on, they heard shots and they thought that she had been killed. However, later on, it turned out that she managed to flee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was indeed a very difficult time that your mother survived. But nevertheless, later on, when she came to Trnopolje, she was transferred to the Bosnian Muslim territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I hope that she is living and well today.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: She's alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that you found refuge in a house of a Ukrainian lady and you stayed there for a month; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. In a house of a Muslim woman, but her house was among the homes of Ukrainians, her neighbours were Ukrainians. This is the wife of Dzemala Sivac, we called her Hada Sivac, she is also alive today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a rather new effect that has come up. Could you please explain to the Court the origin of the Ukrainians around the Prijedor area, they assimilated, their parties affiliations, their religion, so that we will know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I mentioned that in Trnopolje, there were a lot of ethnic groups. I believe there were 17 of them. Among them there were a number of Ukrainians, there were two German families, there were Turks, Albanians, Romalis, Serbs, Croats, and as far as Ukrainians are concerned, I do not know much about their past, or about them. I had some friends at school who were Ukrainians and later on colleagues. I don't know when they had settled there. I know it was in some distant past, but I know that these people whom I knew were born there and they lived and worked on their properties regularly like everybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But isn't it fair to conclude that the Ukrainians' families that created majority in that hamlet were friendly to the SDS or at least you perceived them friendly to SDS?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, that was not my perception. A certain number of Ukrainians managed to escape from the area before the events that we are talking about, and those who did not manage to do so remained there, and out of those some, probably out of fear, agreed to be mobilised. After these events, there were no more Ukrainians left in the village, and I believe that today there are none there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at least it will be -- could we state they were neutral as far as the relationship between SDS and SDA because you sought refuge in that village because there was predominance of the Ukrainians, and Ukrainian who was in the military uniform at that time had given you some information.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not to me. They were neighbours of Ms. Hada who had offered to hide me. I did not make any contact with the Ukrainians, they did not know that I was there. In fact, she was asked at one point, because I guess they had suspected that she was hiding someone and she denied it. Also, I can confirm that there were not many Ukrainians who agreed to be mobilised. It was a small number. And perhaps they did so because they felt that they had to, because they feared for their own lives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Ukrainians in that village where you sought refuge were Orthodox or Catholic or any other religion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They are members of some type, I believe, of a Catholic religion. I think that they call themselves Greek Catholic, I think that's how they define it. I had a colleague in school who was that. But I don't know enough about the distinctions between the Roman Catholic and the Greek Catholic. Whether there were any Orthodox there, that I also do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to move on, and if we could view the tape that the Prosecutor introduced yesterday? Of course, I will not suggest that we view it all, just a few scenes. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, do you recognise the intersection in the background of the picture?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The image that I have on the screen is pretty bad, so I'm not sure that I can see very well what area this is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will direct your attention that this was footage that was taken in and around Trnopolje detention centre. Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I believe this is where the substation, the power substation is, if I see it correctly because, as I said, the image is very bad, and the road could be the Trnopolje-Prijedor road, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Trnopolje-Prijedor road is the stretch of road going from the left edge of the screen to the electrical station here; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that road runs basically east-west?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other road is intersecting the Trnopolje-Prijedor road at 90 degrees, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and it's going in the direction of Kozarac. And the road which we have just described is going towards Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it wouldn't be fair -- strike it. What does this corner represent then that you see in the picture?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is part of the area which was part of the business premises of the agricultural commune, so it was the substation and then, to the right, there were warehouses of this commune and their buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is this electric station, trafo-stanica you called it, that's in the very corner of the property as you described; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at this photo. If you can maybe move it a little bit back and forth so we would get a clearer image? I'm directing your attention, Mr. Semenovic, as the tape is being played, to observe if there is any fence? Could you play it forward now? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any fence at this corner?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Here, on this tape, I cannot see a fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's enough, please. In relation to this corner that we have on tape, could you describe where did you get in and out on few occasions into this camp, because this would be a south-west corner of that detention centre?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It would be the opposite end, over to the right, behind the old cinema building and school building, and on the tape, that would be even farther. The other side that is completely opposite to this side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you inside Trnopolje detention complex, had you ever come close to this corner that you see now in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. But I know this area because my house -- it can almost be seen from this vantage point at the end of this road which you have shown, Prijedor Trnopolje, at the end of that road on the right is my house. You can see a pine tree which is in front of my house, behind this pine tree to the right, at the very pine tree is the entrance to my house, and then behind it is my house, and you cannot see it because there is a lot of greenery covering it. So I knew this area or this terrain quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed. That is indeed very helpful. Based on your recollection prior to -- just immediately prior to the armed conflict around Kozarac in this area, what kind of fence was on this corner, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this part, in this area, when I arrived there, which officially was the camp, in certain parts had a fence, but the fence did not fully surround the compound. This area towards the road did not have a fence, neither before nor during that time when there was a camp there. However, there were machine gun nests there, near my house, and then in this open clear area, on the balcony of Hamdo's house, and then over on the other side on the side where I would enter, behind the road, there was a row of houses between the school building and the house across, there was a barn. This barn was open on both ends. And in this barn, there was also a machine gun nest. The portion that you just showed me, near the place where the camera is standing there was some kind of a bunker and maybe another 50 or 80 metres away from that, there was another military sentry post there, and another further metres along the road there was another sentry post, so this fence was not there along the road, it was on this front side. I don't know how long. Then there was the school fence and the warehouse fence and then there was also a section of the fence where I was entering, from the school and onward, and again there was a clear open space to the house of Hamdo who I have just mentioned. These open spaces were under guard, and these sentry points where these machine gun nests were always manned and somebody was always observing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, you just testified about the position of the machine gun nests?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this very location here, but indeed, just a few moments ago, you testified that while you were in the camp, you never came to this corner. Could you please tell us when did you ascertain a position on those machine guns?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I entered the camp, when I crawled through the canal which I described, I saw the machine gun nests in the barn which I have mentioned. I also saw machine gun nests on the balcony of Hamdo's house, I saw the machine gun nest -- here we go again. Here's the tape. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here to the left of this image, the machine gun nest that I described on the road, I did not personally see, but I contacted about 15 people in the camp and I asked them what the deployment was when the convoys were going and all that stuff. So the majority of people who were there knew about this. I personally did not see it, but other people did. So all this was in one and the same area. But I did mention the ones that I saw personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Place, the exact place, where you entered Trnopolje centre was along this road that we see here but way down west -- I mean -- strike it -- east?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Across from this road. It was behind the substation and the school. It was a lawn. It used to be a soccer field. Parallel to that road, the other end of this soccer field is where I came in; in other words, not this road but the opposite end, the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to make sure that we are talking about the same location, the place where you entered the centre, was it diagonal corner from this corner or the corner which is way to the left as we are looking now on the picture?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the right, not to the left, all the way to the right of the image, and you cannot see that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now we are seeing a man with a wheelbarrow pushing something in a wheelbarrow. Could you tell us what was held in these containers, if you do know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean in the wheelbarrow?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is probably one of the people who had received permission to go home and bring back a sack of flour or something else which he had, because every few days, the police would give permission to a few people to go to their homes and bring wood to build a fire for big caldrons or to bring potatoes if they had any in their back yards, and these permits were issued every several days. However, I do know that they had to receive permission, they had to talk to the guards, and some of them were allowed to go there and some of them were not. However, they all had to come back within a defined period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons under special permission were not escorted by the armed guards to their houses, were they?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I mentioned the road Trnopolje-Kozarac. On that checkpoint, the permits were issued and also the deadline -- the specified time within which they had to come back, and also I heard that close to my house there was a checkpoint as well, and that you could also get permission to leave there and you would go and let them know when you're leaving and they would record the time of departure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But just to be clear, the picture depicting this man is taken inside the camp, not the outside of the camp; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think that a person brought back flour, maybe water from somewhere. I can't see very well on this picture what it is. If it's flour, then based on the permit, he probably went and got it, and if it's water, if it's a water gallon, then the water was probably brought from the pump which was about a hundred metres away, by the school, because this part didn't have really running water and I guess people needed drinking water, so I can't really see what is in the wheelbarrow so I can't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this could be a container in which the water was held for the people in the detention centre; is that correct? Because there was no water in this part of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, there was just the electrical station here, there was no water.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Will you please move on to the next section of the tape? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Further back. You just passed the point that I had some interest in. Could you rewind it, please? Could you rewind it some more? Some more? Right here. Move up a little bit to the point that I indicated to you on the break. Okay. Right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, I am directing your attention to two fences. There is an inner fence and it seems there is an outer fence; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that there is an inner and outer fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe what is the building in the right-hand corner of the picture now as you see it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the building of the old cinema, and it belongs to the complex -- to the compound of the local commune building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that trafo-stanica corner that we just looked earlier in relation to this building?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that storage material building that you indicated earlier in relation to this building?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having lived several years just perhaps 200 yards away, if not less, do you recall what was this fence that is now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was the fence that existed prior to this, before it existed before the one that we can see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was also a fence that was a perimeter of the detention centre, isn't that correct, when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Could you move to the next section of the tape, please? You can fast-forward. Okay. Stop here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see these wheelbarrows here, don't you, Mr. Semenovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The image is not really good, but I do suppose that these are wheelbarrows.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Could you just run the tape back and forth, please, so that we can get a clearer image? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see a little bit better now, Mr. Semenovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the image is really poor, but I do suppose that these are wheelbarrows. They certainly look like wheelbarrows. It's quite possible that they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These wheelbarrows belonged to the building material company, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's possible, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, we should be sure about this. This is Omarska, isn't it, or are you back at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: This is at Trnopolje, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're still at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It's possible that they belonged to the company and also possible that they belonged to the people who were allowed to go out and fetch the flour, and this is why they, after they completed the task, left their wheelbarrows here, but I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the house which is right in the middle of the screen there? Perhaps you lived in that area and you might know whose house that is, the house way in the back.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't see, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a house, as the image is moving, between two blond men in civilian uniforms. It seems they are reporters. Way in the back. Do you recognise that house?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I see the edges, but I guess it's a house of ... I can't see well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Play it a little further. Slow. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Could you stop it here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the tree line in the back here?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand. I do see that these are the trees --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this particular cluster of trees, having lived there for so long and having been at the camp, detention centre for a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that these trees are those that are located on the road in the direction of Prijedor. I think that it's in the vicinity of the house of -- Hamdo's house that I've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Could you move it to the next -- quickly to the next piece, section of the tape? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Could you slowly now play that part of the tape from here? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: You can play it normal speed, I didn't mean slow, just play it normal speed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Semenovic, I'm directing your attention to the people that are next to the fence and the people that are getting out. That's enough. Thank you. Mr. Semenovic, did you recognise that part of the fence there in the picture now?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that this is the fence by the road, Trnopolje-Kozarac. I think that's what it is. And across from this fence are the houses, mostly Ukrainian houses, in which at that point still some Ukrainians resided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me at this point at least, in the detention centre, the people are walking in and out freely, were they?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. I think -- I suppose that these people on the road are the people that actually live in the houses that I have mentioned, in the houses across from the camp. There was a family of Pavle, the Ukrainian who was there, and also some other families who lived there for a while before they departed as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we've seen two civilians, two young girls, walking out?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the people, about the families that actually lived there. I suppose that these are those families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please play the tape back again? Only with the civilians getting out of the -- the section of the fence where the civilians are getting out. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: A little more. Could you back it up just a bit more? You can play it at a normal speed from here. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you direct your attention, Mr. Semenovic, to the man walking now in the picture? The girl coming out, the second girl coming out. Thank you. You can stop playing this footage. Mr. Semenovic, do you recognise the man, elderly man, who walked in on that part of the film?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise. I don't know who it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified about Ukrainian men having a house just across the street. Are these girls that walked out part of the household?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't recognise the exact persons. I have just said that in these houses across from the camp at that point there was still some people residing there, and also the people from the Serbian Red Cross from Prijedor visited the camp as well and there were civilians. Also the treatment was different for men and women in Trnopolje. The men were treated much, much more strictly. And they were not allowed to leave the camp without permission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the elderly gentleman who we saw in this footage seemed like he was bringing something in a container to the centre, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Could you play that part of the tape back, please? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: You can play it from here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are two uniformed men right on the road now, as you see, and there's a man with a white T-shirt coming out carrying a container in his right hand.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think he was going to fetch the water into one of those Ukrainian houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to conclude that was one of the detainees or the refugees at this centre going to get water at this time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is possible, but I'm not sure because I don't know this particular person and he must have had permission because otherwise he wouldn't have been able to go there. I know that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Go to the next segment of the tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that this man is Mr. Kupresanin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position in the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time when the coalition government was formed in the beginning of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a member of the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, just like me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in the leadership of the SDS, on the State level?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had any communications with him, any conferences, either professional or social in terms of determining the policy, or trying to do a better job as a legislator or any conversations with him in the beginning of 1991?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have seen him in the parliament and I have listened to him talk just like other legislators from other parties. We didn't have any particular contact, nor did we carry on any particular conversations. He was just a member of the parliament just like me, and since I was a legislator as well, I've seen a lot of these people, sometimes I would listen to their speeches, sometimes I would listen to the conversations they had with other people, just like they listened to mine, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yet this man, Mr. Kupresanin, later 4 became the president of the autonomous region of Serb 5 Krajina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were confined in Omarska, he came in to see you, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he didn't come to see me. From what I understood, he came to look for the officials, highly placed officials that were still alive, and he wanted to gather them at one point in Banja Luka, and he coordinated that with the higher leaders, he had some consultations with Karadzic on that issue, and the purpose was to use those surviving highly-placed officials for their own purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just from their actions it would be fair to say that Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Kupresanin thought that the SDA leaders in Omarska are not at great peril because he came to contact them, as one of the conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEMENOVIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Two days later, I found out exactly what their intentions were. One Serbian soldier who escorted me from the municipal building where I was taken by the police, when he escorted me back to Vrbanja in the car, at one point the soldier told me, "Your decision to become a member of the Serbian parliament was a good one. I appreciate that. However, you have to be aware the Muslim extremists can kill you." And it was completely clear what was actually taking place in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Tadic's trial, you testified on page 961 that, starting on line 20 to 26. Did Mr. Kupresanin ever ask you to assist in negotiations? You answered: Yes, yes. One of the first things that they wanted to do was they wanted to create some kind of roundtable in Banja Luka. He said as follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't go too quickly. It's got to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: ... is going to be the part Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is of the Banja Luka region -- Your Honours, I lost the sound on my earphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
